title: Inkább... Mint...: Preferring One Option, Gently

sections.title: Naming a preference without deciding for anyone
sections.content: You already know inkább ("rather"). Put a conditional-mood verb in front of it and add mint ("than") before the option you're not choosing, and you get a soft, personal preference rather than a decision handed down: Én inkább X-et választanám, mint Y-t states what you would pick, leaving the real choice with the listener — the same gentle register as -hat/-het suggestions in Lesson 2.

items.spanish: Én inkább a biztonságos utat választanám, mint a gyorsabbat.
items.english: I would rather choose the safe route than the faster one.

items.spanish: A te helyedben inkább várnék egy kicsit, mint azonnal döntenék.
items.english: In your place, I'd rather wait a bit than decide right away.

items.spanish: Inkább most beszélnél vele, mint később?
items.english: Would you rather talk to him/her now than later?

sections.content: mint here introduces the option being passed over, not a full clause of its own — a döntenék, mint azonnal döntenék pattern (verb ... mint verb) is completely normal and doesn't need a second subject repeated after mint.
